infosec.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script

Attackers received about $2.64 million in POL from 33 wallets within 52 minutes. Polymarket is refunding $3.9 million, including $2.7 million to 726 affected wallets. The breach involved a compromised laptop and malware that deleted evidence. Binance has replenished 90% of stolen assets and pledged to cover the remainder. The FBI warns that stolen funds are being converted into Ethereum and laundered through DeFi and instant swap services.

infosec.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
infosec.summary: VOLTA takes a "steal everything, let AI sort it out" approach: it grabs credentials, sessions, wallets, and cloud keys, then uses the victim's own Gmail, DoorDash, and Discord sessions to confirm details like a home address. It sends the resulting dossier through OpenRouter to Claude, falling back to Kimi and then Gemini if a model refuses, and gets back a ranked "WHAT THEY'RE WORTH" assessment of what the victim's assets could fetch. Talos assessed VOLTA as a commodity builder that runs entirely on third-party infrastructure. They recommended that defenders block or alert on non-developer processes launching Chrome with --headless, since that is how the stealer gets around App-Bound Encryption.

infosec.title: Discovering a Backdoor and Flaws in More Encrypted USB Drives
infosec.summary: Vector 35 researcher Xusheng Li pointed Codex at Binary Ninja's MCP server and recovered the keys hardcoded in NetacFileLock, KakaSoft USB Copy Protection, and Nexcopy Copy Secure in 7 to 26 minutes each. In each product, the key was fixed in the binary, derived from an embedded seed, or unlocked by a certificate in the viewer, so the user's password never protected the files. Separately, time-travel debugging turned up two hidden accounts in SecZure's YutianDun drive, with passwords as weak as "123456", that could decrypt any file. Li skipped vendor disclosure because drives already in the field can't be patched, and he argued that client-side validation is never secure, so buyers should only trust drives that derive their encryption key from the user's password.

infosec.title: Agentic Offensive Frameworks Hit Real Intrusions
infosec.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant observed intruders using the open-source ARTEX framework with stolen credentials and letting its six sub-agents run Azure and AWS permission sweeps, Kerberoasting, DCSync, and MySQL log poisoning that wrote JSP webshells in bursts as short as 2 to 25 seconds. ARTEX users included financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters such as UNC7228, which went from a first account to deep access in about four hours, though GTIG noted the agents were forensically noisy and sometimes undid each other's work. Mandiant recommended short-lived, tightly scoped credentials, locking down admin interfaces like Kudu/SCM as privileged infrastructure, and behavioral detection tuned for machine-speed bursts.

infosec.title: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux

Attackers targeted Alpine Linux on October 20 to 21, crashed worker processes, and downloaded its container image. Alpine found no confirmed code execution or repository tampering, rebuilt the instance, and reset passwords. CISA added the bug to KEV. GitLab-only updates may be insufficient for custom Ruby deployments. Use Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9, or later.

The authors then showcase a selection of regulations with provisions lacking proper citations, which could render them void and unenforceable.

infosec.title: CVE-2026-98432: which Linux kernels are still vulnerable
infosec.summary: Mattias Geniar found 712 Multipath TCP listeners on his own Ubuntu 26.04 laptop, opened without his knowledge by Go programs like tailscaled, because Go 1.24 and later enable MPTCP on listening sockets by default. That matters because the only known exploit for CVE-2026-98432 needs an MPTCP listener. The bug is a use-after-free in the kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake that dates back to Linux 4.4 and can be reached with a single SYN. Upstream stable kernels were fixed in mid-October, and Debian, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK have shipped patches, but Ubuntu and RHEL still had no fixed kernel as of November 1.

data.title: Do you even benchmark? How we evaluate agents at scale
data.summary: PostHog tests AI agents on real tasks, such as finding the bugs behind 33 past incidents, where its review agent caught 62%, or checking whether playback failures affected real users. It isolates each test so agents cannot copy earlier answers and is building resettable environments with fixed data to make comparisons fair.

data.title: Vector Search on Apache Iceberg Without Moving Source Data
data.summary: StarTree adapts Pinot's HNSW vector index for Iceberg tables, keeping Parquet source records in object storage while storing and serving a derived index alongside them. This enables hybrid similarity and SQL-filtered queries without a second copy of the records. The trade-off: indexes are roughly as large as the embeddings, and freshness follows Iceberg snapshot synchronization rather than real-time ingestion.

data.title: Move the elephant, keep the lights on
data.summary: Logical replication lets you upgrade or migrate PostgreSQL with only seconds of downtime: run the target cluster in parallel, stream changes, then cut over when ready. Its real advantage over in-place upgrades is rollback safety and cross-environment portability. Plan around what it does not move automatically, especially schema changes and sequences.

data.title: What Happened to Data Products?
data.summary: Data products outlasted data-mesh hype by becoming a delivery discipline rather than an enterprise reorganisation: a governed output, accountable owner, defined consumer, and evidence of value. AI agents raise the stakes because they cannot recover missing context through informal knowledge. Start with a business-critical workflow, then make meaning, quality, access, and permitted use machine-readable.

data.title: ParticleDB 1.1.4
data.summary: Jepsen found 96 issues in ParticleDB, including data loss, crashes, and incorrect SQL results, mostly without any server failures. Most were fixed during testing, but serious transaction bugs remained. Orkes says a newer release fixes them, though Jepsen has not verified this.

data.title: 46% more accurate when your agent stops reading the drafts
data.summary: Nobody deletes anything from SharePoint, so your agent reads old versions, contradictions, half-finished files and rogue customer data. Deasy qualifies every file and keeps the bad ones out of reach. Takes minutes. Works for every agent after that. See it →

data.title: Kafgres 0.2.0: 700 MB/s Kafka-Compatible Streaming Inside Postgres
data.summary: Kafgres, a Kafka-compatible Postgres extension, reached about 700 MB/s after caching query plans, relaxing commit durability, and replacing timer-based polling with socket readiness checks. It could suit many workloads, but the single-broker setup lacks the resilience of a Kafka cluster spread across availability zones.

data.title: Nodal Analytics
data.summary: Nodal is an open-source toolkit that turns analysts' business definitions into reusable context for AI analytics agents. It plans queries and checks results against approved metrics, filters, and joins, flagging uncertainty for expert review.

data.title: Primary Keys Come to Apache Iceberg V4, and Most of Them Start Out Unenforced
data.summary: Apache Iceberg V4 adds primary keys, unique rules, and checks, such as requiring positive order amounts, though most will initially be unenforced. Each snapshot records whether the data meets those rules, separately from whether writers must enforce them on new writes.

data.title: I Told an AI Agent That Its Wrong Answers Were Right. One Model Believed Me
data.summary: In most cases, flipping the reward labels in an agent's memory barely changes how it learns. This test hid a rule only the labels could reveal. With true labels, GPT-6 Sol scored 94.4 out of 100 on its last six trials, and with flipped labels 7.8. Claude Haiku 5.5 improved less, and Qwen3 4B barely moved.

data.title: Active-Active Oracle GoldenGate Across Regions: Decide Who Owns the Data Before You Resolve Conflict
data.summary: Active-active GoldenGate only works when data ownership and conflict policy are designed table by table before replication starts. Simulations showed that even convergent strategies like last-writer-wins can silently lose updates, while delta merging preserves each decrement but cannot prevent both regions from accepting a request against the same last unit before replication catches up. The lesson is blunt: if business rules cannot tolerate reconciliation, do not rely on multi-master replication to fix the problem later.

data.title: What Five P99 CONF Talks Reveal About Database Trade-offs
data.summary: A sponsored P99 CONF round-up exposes the costs behind several database designs: object storage trades low-cost durability for cold-read latency, read-optimized engines trade RAM and write amplification for tail latency, and vector search trades quantization and cache complexity for scale. The reported benchmarks are workload-specific, but the recurring lesson is: removing one bottleneck moves the constraint elsewhere.

data.title: Upgrading MLflow Pipelines Across a Python Version Boundary
data.summary: Moving Databricks from Python 3.10 to 3.12 broke Zalando's pickled MLflow models.

data.title: Your backups are green. That does not mean you can restore
data.summary: Successful PostgreSQL backups can still fail to restore because of missing transaction logs, copied corruption, or lost encryption keys.

design.title: WhatsApp group chats get permanent message pins, private Status updates, and more
design.summary: WhatsApp is adding four features designed to make busy group conversations easier to manage, including permanent message pins and Group Status updates visible only to members of a particular group. A new filter collects unread conversations containing mentions, direct replies, or @all messages so users can quickly find messages that need their attention. Recent message history can also now be shared with someone after they have joined a group, helping new members catch up without exposing older conversations automatically.

design.title: Meta Quietly Launches an AI Fashion App Called Style Sketch
design.summary: Meta's Style Sketch is an AI app that builds a virtual closet from a user's Instagram photos and suggests outfits from clothes they already own. Virtual try-ons use a model reflecting the user's body shape and skin tone, and trip plans pack outfits around destination, activities, and weather. The app launched on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand, with no word on a wider rollout.

design.title: The iPad is Finally Getting the Affinity App Creatives Have Been Asking For
design.summary: Affinity's all-in-one creative app is finally coming to iPad, nearly a year after its desktop debut, answering long-standing demands since new-format files can't open in the older V2 iPad apps. It combines photo editing, vector design, page layout, and sketching, with Apple Pencil support for pressure, tilt, and barrel roll, plus RAW editing and formats like PSD, AI, INDD, and SVG. The app is free for individuals despite its “pre-order” label, though Canva AI Studio features require a premium plan.

design.title: “This wasn't a thoughtfully designed menu.”
design.summary: Hawaii's 2018 false missile alert demonstrates how poor information architecture, ambiguous labels, and insufficient friction can turn an interface mistake into a real-world emergency affecting 1.4 million people. The alert system reportedly placed confusingly named test and real commands together without clear hierarchy or confirmation proportional to the consequences, making a catastrophic selection surprisingly easy. The same principles apply to everyday software on a smaller scale: visually similar choices, weak labeling, and poorly structured menus create countless small errors that gradually erode usability and trust.

design.title: There Will Always Be Someone Faster, Cheaper, and Better
design.summary: AI intensifies designers' fears about competing with people who can work faster, cheaper, or better, but those pressures have existed throughout the history of professional design and every major shift in production tools. Faster tools become threatening when designers price their time rather than outcomes, while “better” extends beyond the quality of an artifact to the experience, perspective, judgment, and relationships a designer brings to a client. As AI makes production faster, deliberately taking time to gain experience, make mistakes, and develop a singular way of working may become more valuable than racing to master whichever tool is currently dominant.

design.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default
design.summary: Slow design system components make every app built on them slow, so performance belongs next to accessibility on the team's priority list. Timing ten popular systems on a 249-country dropdown and 100 checkboxes found Fluent and Carbon quickest to open the dropdown and Ionic by far the slowest. Playwright tests with explicit budgets, virtualized long lists, and published performance numbers keep components fast by default.

design.title: Automate Video Creation with AI Agent
design.summary: An AI video agent that turns your ideas, documents, links, and media assets into share-ready videos. Describe the video you want to make, upload your assets, and Cutbay helps you shape the idea.

design.title: A Library of Patterns and Principles for Inventing New Interfaces
design.summary: An interlinked library that takes interfaces apart for the people who make them. Every entry names the mechanism, traces it back to the people who built it, and connects it to the ideas it grew from.

design.title: Free Online PDF Accessibility Checker
design.summary: Check the accessibility of your PDF against WCAG and PDF/UA. Get actionable recommendations to fix the issues and move toward ADA, Section 508, and EAA compliance.

design.title: Website Design that Converts: Why Good-Looking Sites Still Fail
design.summary: Striking photography wins attention but fails when visitors cannot tell what working with a studio involves. Dutch lighting consultancy Eclectic Lighting bridges that gap with sector-based project filters, a four-step process, specific client reviews, and a floor plan upload. Asking for a floor plan visitors already have turns the contact form into a concrete next step.

design.title: COPUS and Kontrapunkt design JUNO the bakery's cookie brand and site
design.summary: Kontrapunkt extended Copenhagen's JUNO the bakery into a restrained identity and packaging system built around white paper, subtle blue accents, simple duotone illustrations, and the bakery's blue peacock mascot. Its Danish Butter Cookies use the same quiet visual language. COPUS and Tommy Campbell carried the identity into JUNO's first online shop, using blue sparingly for highlights, product tiles, and the add-to-cart button to make the digital experience feel like a window into the physical bakery.

design.title: I Gave My Website a Boss Fight
design.summary: Missing the personality of the old internet, Paul Bakaus rebuilt his personal website over ten days with Claude Code as a retro Amiga-style world, using a 4,096-color palette, live-synthesized music, and a boss fight against a monster called Jirasaurus. Each page became a themed scene, from a rooftop panel and a speaking auditorium to a floppy-disk office platformer, and three pages hide playable games. Claude wrote the code, built the art pipeline, and composed the music, but animation needed a leg rig and constant feedback, and the site stays a fast, optional-to-play Ghost theme where reading still comes first.

design.title: This Horse-Shaped Headset Asks Designers to See the World Through Animal Eyes
design.summary: Equine Eyes, an oversized horse-head headset, uses side-mounted cameras and a VR display to simulate a horse's nearly 350-degree field of view and blue-yellow color perception.

design.title: This Artist is Using 90s Anime Aesthetics to Create the Ultimate Nostalgic Masterpieces That Will Hit You Right in the Feels
design.summary: Japanese-American illustrator Mike Yoshimura channels 80s and 90s anime, retro cyberpunk, and vintage cel animation into solitary figures in neon-lit rain and twilight cityscapes.

design.title: How this artist turned childhood nightmares into video game monsters
design.summary: John Kenn Mortensen translated his hand-drawn creatures and childhood fascination with darkness into the fantasy roguelike FLASK, combining grotesque medieval imagery, black humor, Labyrinth-like fantasy, and the energy of Slayer while working with a game art team to preserve his distinctive style in a colorful digital world.

marketing.title: Majority of teens and tweens now use chat bots, new research finds
marketing.summary: AI chatbots are becoming a normal part of life for American teens and tweens. Nearly half of 9-12-year-olds have bypassed the 13+ age restrictions. Students use chatbots for homework and emotional support. A separate study of 5,000+ students found that using AI during emotional distress is associated with worse mental health outcomes. Researchers have not established whether AI contributes to these issues or attracts students already struggling.

marketing.title: AI Search Is Growing Faster Than Its Business Model
marketing.summary: AI search is growing faster than platforms can monetize it, prompting Google and OpenAI to expand conversational ads. Google search queries grew at their fastest rate in 5 years while ad revenue growth slowed to 12%. More ads could erode trust in AI-generated answers, which 70% of regular users in the US and UK currently trust.

marketing.title: Run your tongue across your teeth
marketing.summary: Claude Hopkins built Pepsodent's campaign around a problem customers could recognize, using a 3 second test to demonstrate sticky film on teeth. He offered free samples with instructions to test the toothpaste's effectiveness. Unique coupon codes helped track headline performance and revealed that leading with “free” reduced response by 75%. He also tested campaigns in one city before expanding nationally.

marketing.title: Chunking your content for agent readability
marketing.summary: Chunking breaks documentation into smaller passages that AI agents retrieve independently, so each section needs to make sense without the full page. Keep sections under your retrieval system's token limit (Google's Agent Search defaults to 500 tokens) and use specific headings with proper HTML tags. Break up long tables and procedures into smaller sections. Keep code samples self-contained and describe important images in text. Test how your content is actually chunked using an agent skill or retrieval system API.

marketing.title: How to test incrementality before peak spending starts
marketing.summary: Run incrementality tests before peak season to identify which marketing channels actually generate new sales rather than taking credit for purchases that would happen anyway. Use geographic or audience holdouts to compare exposed customers against groups that don't see a channel. Aim for 20-30% holdouts and run tests for 4-8 weeks. Audit UTMs and tracking before launch. Use incremental ROAS and new customer acquisition to reallocate budget toward channels that drive genuine lift rather than those reporting the highest last-click revenue.

marketing.title: PR in an AI era: Building authority where it matters
marketing.summary: How will your brand earn visibility and trust? Join IDHL on 19 November to explore why Brand PR and Digital PR need to work together to build the authority needed to be found, understood and chosen. Join the webinar

marketing.title: The Website Go‑Live Checklist: 5 Critical Checks Beyond Good Looks
marketing.summary: Before launching a website, review it from the customer's perspective to ensure the offer is clear and visitors can easily find information and take action. Check that the design works on mobile without unnecessary scrolling or distracting elements. Score clarity, branding, and usability against specific criteria rather than relying on subjective feedback. Use tools like Loom or Tella to record and track revisions.

marketing.title: How we run our newsletters on beehiiv's MCP
marketing.summary: Strategy Breakdowns uses beehiiv's MCP integration with Claude Code to automate newsletter production. Claude analyzes hundreds of past A/B tests to identify winning subject line patterns. Testing 4 variations before sending to the full list increased open rates by at least 1.24 percentage points. It also segments subscribers and researches topics using trusted chart sources. A custom dashboard called SB Dash connects these workflows and automates sponsor reporting. This cut production tasks from 2-3 hours per edition to 10 minutes a day. Human editors still write every word.

marketing.title: Why AI Fails In Marketing: The Organizational Problem Leaders Overlook
marketing.summary: AI in marketing mostly fails for organizational reasons, not technical ones. Marketing owns revenue and retention targets but rarely controls pricing or product, so AI insights go unused. The highest-value uses also depend on sales, finance, and product sharing goals and data. Judged on cost savings alone, marketing AI tools just makes ineffective activities cheaper, not more effective.

marketing.title: Nobody Yet Knows How to Measure an Ad Inside a Chatbot Answer
marketing.summary: Ads in ChatGPT and Google AI Mode reach consumers while they're expressing purchase intent, but neither platform can prove they generate incremental sales. Conversion tracking shows which purchases follow an ad but not whether they would have happened anyway. Facebook research found observational measurement can misstate results by 3X or more. Treat AI ads as an experimental channel and use geographic holdouts to measure their actual impact until platforms offer randomized lift studies.

founders.title: The return of the full-stack app
founders.summary: Emerging AI app startups resemble infrastructure companies by training their own models and managing complex workflows, enhancing technical depth. Four key changes favor these startups: owning models, handling complex and costly agent operations, prioritizing security and governance, and building customer trust. Successful AI app companies focus on delivering outcomes, specialize in high-stakes verticals, integrate organization-wide workflows, and incorporate deep technical infrastructure.

founders.title: Principles for Building Effective Vertical AI Products
founders.summary: Vertical AI takes the workflows of the best practitioners and codifies them into agentic systems that deliver capability, quality, and efficiency a third-party frontier model can't match. The challenge is finding workflows and translating them into products, context layers, agentic harnesses, data systems, and feedback loops. Seamless transition requires an organization and culture that brings world-class GTM and engineering to the same table every day. The organization's people need to speak a common language and rapidly build based on that shared vernacular and best practices.

founders.title: How to give AI company context and build a company brain
founders.summary: Ramp recommends a one-to-two-page context document paired with live connectors to the tools where work happens, arguing AI gives confident but wrong answers because it cannot guess internal definitions, policies, and workflows. The guide compares five ways to supply context, from custom instructions to fine-tuning, and advises setting permissions first, testing with 10 to 20 known-answer questions, and assigning owners. Ramp says its most AI-forward staff kept personal setups few colleagues saw, which led to its Glass workspace.

It assesses identity and looks for signs of fraud, bringing the findings together in one place. Teams are able to see how risks develop across the hiring process and spot patterns that individual checks might miss. It can spot fake applications, detect deepfakes and proxy candidates in live interviews, and verify government ID.

founders.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
founders.summary: Cloudflare services for private origins connects internal services to the Internet without exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin. founders.summary: Gemini in Google Slides can now be used to edit multiple slides or an entire presentation with a single prompt. It can update content throughout a deck, refresh visual styles in bulk, or match the style of another presentation. The AI determines which slides need to change and applies edits directly. Users stay in full control and can make further adjustments. Gemini displays a summary of the changes in the side panel after it finishes editing.

founders.title: Our Core Vendor Was Down for 24 Hours. Our AI Agent Replaced Them Before They Came Back Up
founders.summary: AI has made outages even more risky for businesses as replacements are now easier to source. Humans may wait for a vendor to fix their services, but agents making less emotional and more calculating decisions may choose to switch vendors or build in-house solutions much sooner. Vendors that communicate poorly during incidents will lose the most customers. Their customers' agents will build or suggest replacements, and there will be nothing to save by the time renewal comes up.

founders.title: The Software Factory as Identity Defense (and Reinvention)
founders.summary: Software factories are becoming more and more appealing to engineers trying to preserve their role as AI makes coding cheaper. The cloud put operations teams in a similar position in 2012 when Netflix described needing few of them and an Etsy employee called “NoOps” “the dumbest marketing term ever coined in my field.” Someone still had to build the platforms that let developers serve themselves. Engineers building agent factories are making a similar move, taking control of the quality standards and deployment systems that determine which code reaches customers.

crypto.title: Chainalysis says hacker using ‘offensive agentic techniques' accessed its customers' names and emails
crypto.summary: An unidentified AI-assisted hacker accessed “non-sensitive” customer data, including user IDs, full names, emails, and role labels. Chainalysis says it has found no sign that investigation content, query results, plaintext passwords, MFA secrets, or session tokens were accessed. It did not say when the intrusion occurred, how many customers were affected, or how AI agents were used. It says the breach is unrelated to the Binance hack. Separately, Chainalysis puts the Binance theft at $6.4B, attributed to North Korean groups. It says the attackers are using automation to cycle funds between addresses and using JustLend on Tron to get around stablecoin freezes. About $2.8B in stablecoins has already been frozen.

crypto.title: Binance Security Incident Update #3: 90% of Stolen Assets Replenished
crypto.summary: Binance has reached 90% replenishment of the $6.3B drained from its hot wallets on October 29, when attackers compromised a DevOps engineer's laptop to access internal signing services. All top-10 assets (BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC) are now 100% backed. The remaining 10% covers less-liquid tokens outside the top 10 that are harder to source at volume. Binance funded the replenishment through partial SAFU deployment, a portion of the Futures insurance fund, and corporate treasury, and took a new Proof of Reserves snapshot at October 31 00:00 UTC, with the ZK proof expected by November 3. Withdrawal services are scheduled to reopen November 1, with Binance absorbing all financial losses and users facing no shortfall.

crypto.title: Ephemeral Rollup: The New "L1.5" of Ethereum
crypto.summary: A proposed "L1.5" pattern for Ethereum separates stateless compute from state by placing user secrets in wallets and commitments, nullifiers, and verifiers on L1, so rollup-style execution can run without any long-lived operator holding user state. Three forthcoming EIPs enable this: EIP-8141 frame transactions let contracts self-pay fees after verifying a proof, EIP-8250 keyed nonces repurpose privacy nullifiers to reject double spends, and EIP-8288 aggregates proofs so the block carries a single recursive proof checked once per node. Any prover can take an L1.5 job (a stateless function over L1 state and user inputs) so long as its output is checked by L1, its fee is paid without linking payer identity, and submission requires no dedicated sequencer. Target applications include gasless payments via threshold-blind-signed tickets, fair exchange for private RPC and PIR queries, and stealth privacy pools, with a three-step migration path for existing L2 apps: move owned state into wallets, enable contracts to issue their own VERIFY-frame transactions, and open proving and submission to any party.

crypto.title: Stripe Powers Stablecoin Deposits in Walmart's OnePay
crypto.summary: Stripe's Bridge platform now powers USDC deposits into OnePay, Walmart's consumer financial services app, letting select US customers fund checking accounts from external wallets or exchanges across 12 chains, including Base, Solana, and Ethereum. Bridge handles deposit address generation, compliance checks, and USDC-to-USD conversion, with balances credited within moments and no conversion fees at launch. The integration targets gig workers and cross-border earners who receive USDC and want to access those funds through a mainstream banking product without holding a separate stablecoin balance. OnePay describes this as the first of several stablecoin-enabled features planned for the platform, signaling a broader buildout of crypto rails inside Walmart's fintech stack.

crypto.title: Non-USD stablecoins are one of the most underrated segments
crypto.summary: A key neobank use is avoiding FX fees, since paying in another currency often costs over 1%, and local stablecoins with multi-currency settlement can remove that. The main problem is fragmentation, with many issuers per currency, such as six for the real, three for the yen, and three for the Swiss franc, plus several for EURC-type euro coins. Questions remain around how many guarantee 1:1 backing or can be verified in real time, and the industry may benefit from less issuer competition.

crypto.title: Binance $6.3B Hack: Would Your Perp DEX Be Safer?
crypto.summary: On October 29, a hacked DevOps laptop gave attackers access to Binance's internal signing system, which approved an EIP-7702 delegation handing hot wallet control to the attacker's contract, draining $6.3B with no private key compromise required and $3B since frozen. The same vector cost Bitget $350M a month earlier, both exploiting signing systems configured with blocklists rather than allowlists that permit only known-good transactions. Hyperliquid holds $5.6B of its $6.5B USDC in a Coinbase-controlled treasury address moved by unsigned system transactions, meaning a single key or validator compromise reaches the bulk of user funds. Lighter ($1B, Ethereum) uses ZK proofs to verify withdrawals with a 14-day forced-exit escape hatch, the only DEX among four analyzed where server compromise alone cannot drain balances, though its 4-of-7 security council bypassed upgrade-notice requirements five times in October.

crypto.title: This Week on Base: Denim, $243M Card Spend, 20+ Launches
crypto.summary: Base's Denim upgrade, its fourth network update of 2026, was deployed to Sepolia ahead of a November 5 mainnet activation that cuts block times to 200ms. Card spend settled on Base hit $243M in October, an 80% increase from March, and Coinbase Tokenized Stocks crossed $4B in all-time DEX trading volume on the network. FalconX launched an institutional USDC credit facility on Base, Ripple deployed RLUSD liquidity, and PeerXYZ opened an Alipay beta for USDC acquisition against CNY payments. Y Combinator paid a $500K MochaTrade investment in USDC on Base and published a Crypto Request for Startups targeting AI agents, stablecoins, capital raising, and trading.

crypto.title: The Lenders Behind Curator Vaults
crypto.summary: RWA.xyz's analysis of $6.1B in Morpho variable-rate stablecoin lending identifies supply, not borrowing demand, as the binding growth constraint, with five curators (Steakhouse, Sentora, Gauntlet, SparkDAO, and RockawayX) overseeing 80%+ ($5.0B) of deployed capital. Of the $2.6B traced to specific funding sources, platform earn integrations and Sky-authorized protocol balance sheets each account for $1.1B, with issuer reserve lending via Ethena and similar protocols contributing the rest. Platform earn integrations offer the most expandable near-term growth vector, while credit limits cap protocol balance sheet allocations and redemption liquidity requirements constrain issuer reserve portfolios. For tokenized collateral, transfer restrictions, redemption terms, and secondary-market liquidity under stress set the ceiling on lender capacity.

crypto.title: 50 companies worth over $25 trillion object to tokenization on OKXICE

crypto.summary: Aave October revenue is annualizing at about $77M.

fintech.summary: Binance said October 30 that it has reserved corporate funds to restore customer balances after attackers exploited internal withdrawal systems, while partners separately froze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. fintech.title: AI agents won't pay the way you do
fintech.summary: AI agents could materially change the payment mix because they will optimize for user-defined goals such as rewards, discounts, cost, and efficiency rather than simply following familiar checkout habits. That could favor methods like pay-by-bank in some contexts and create a new competition among cards, bank payments, and other rails to become the payment option agents select on behalf of consumers.

fintech.title: AI Is Coming for Billable Hours. Intuit Turns Accountants Into Growth Advisors
fintech.summary: New tools will automate month-end close, flag financial anomalies, and let firms build custom agents, freeing up time for higher-value client work. According to the company, its Accountant Suite serves more than 260,000 firms, with users reporting savings of over nine hours per client each month and many spending 30% more time on advisory services. The platform will also match growing businesses with firms, helping them replace revenue from routine tasks with advice and new client relationships.

fintech.title: Apple Pay and Google Pay launch in Uzbekistan
fintech.summary: Uzbekistan has announced the arrival of Apple Pay and Google Pay into its banking system as the Central Asian nation looks to open up its financial services.

fintech.title: CD&R targets $40B buyout of Global Payments
fintech.summary: Private equity firm CD&R is reportedly working with Global Payments' largest shareholder, GTCR, on a potential take-private of the payments processor, which has an enterprise value of about $40 billion. The talks come after Global Payments' $22.7 billion Worldpay acquisition drew investor criticism and activist pressure, making a private-equity-led reset a possible next step if a deal materializes.

fintech.title: ICE moves to bring Hyperliquid perpetual futures to the US
fintech.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the NYSE, signed a deal with Trade[XYZ] to operate regulated US markets for perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid, with ICE also taking a strategic stake in the company. The planned offering would bring 24/7 leveraged perpetuals on assets such as stocks, commodities and currencies into a regulated US framework using KYC, futures brokers and ICE clearing infrastructure, marking a significant bridge between crypto-native market structure and traditional exchanges.

fintech.title: Harlem Children's Zone buys Goalsetter to enhance financial education offering
fintech.summary: The New York nonprofit plans to extend the platform's student-focused tools into a continuous learning journey from early childhood through adulthood. Its existing products include classroom modules for middle and high schools and MoneyLingo, an app teaching college students and young adults about saving, spending, investing, and credit. Founder Tanya Van Court will join HCZ as chief fintech officer. Financial terms were not disclosed.

fintech.title: Brian Armstrong says crypto and AI can rebuild the financial system
fintech.summary: Crypto will replace financial rails through stablecoins, tokenization, and 24/7 onchain markets, while AI will replace the interface by letting agents research, decide, transact, and pay for users.

fintech.title: Visa signs digital payments deal with Senegal
fintech.summary: Visa and Senegal's Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishing a two-year framework for strategic collaboration to support Senegal's digital transformation ambitions.

it.title: When an employee leaves, do their passwords leave with them?
it.summary: Shared logins are a fact of life in most orgs. Today, they're also shared by AI agents. That means business-critical automations are running on someone's credentials. What happens when that someone quits? Cue the frantic search through spreadsheets, browsers, and Slack DMs... Keeper puts every password and passkey in one zero-knowledge encrypted vault, so IT can see what exists, who has access, and lock it down when someone leaves. Zero-trust, zero-knowledge security Quick to set up, with 24/7 support Trusted by over 100,000 businesses Protect your organization from cyber threats and save 30% on Business Starter for a limited time only .

it.title: Google Cloud lets teams cap project spending
it.summary: Google Cloud has made spend caps generally available for eligible services. Teams can use the Cloud Billing Budgets API to give every new sandbox project a spending limit, then raise or remove it when a developer needs more room.

it.title: AI is finding bugs faster than PostgreSQL maintainers can review fixes
it.summary: A surge in AI-assisted bug reports and patches helped push PostgreSQL 19 past its usual fall release window. Maintainers still have to verify proposed fixes and apply them to older versions. The project is targeting November 19 for release.

it.title: Linux 7.4 sets a record with nearly 20,000 commits
it.summary: The Linux 7.4 merge window drew nearly 20,000 commits, the busiest in kernel history. For comparison, Linux 7.3 took its entire release cycle to reach 20,260 commits.

it.title: Five years after the fork, who steers OpenSearch?
it.summary: AWS created OpenSearch after Elastic changed the license for Elasticsearch. Elastic has since restored an open-source licensing option, but the projects have continued to diverge. This post examines where OpenSearch has taken its own technical direction and how much influence AWS still holds over its governance.

it.title: Andy Jassy thinks Bedrock could become as big as EC2
it.summary: Amazon's CEO argues that companies will want to switch AI models as price and performance change. His bet is that giving customers one place to run models from several vendors could make Bedrock as large a business as EC2, AWS' core computing service.

it.title: ServiceNow brings OpenAI, Anthropic, and Okta into its AI governance alliance
it.summary: ServiceNow launched the Control Tower Alliance with 11 founding partners spanning AI models, cloud infrastructure, identity, and security. Members plan to deliver pretested integrations so customers can use ServiceNow's Control Tower to govern AI systems from multiple vendors.

it.title: Tencent connects WorkBuddy to ERP and CRM systems
it.summary: Tencent's WorkBuddy office agent can now query business systems through the Model Context Protocol. An employee can ask for a report that draws on both customer and operations data, and the agent can break the request into steps, retrieve records from each system, and present the findings.

it.title: How Docusign teaches agents to read amended contracts
it.summary: Figuring out what a company owes a supplier can mean reconciling the signed contract with three amendments, a revised price schedule, and an internal purchasing policy. In this interview, CTO Sagnik Nandy explains how the company gives its Iris agents the context to answer that kind of question.

it.title: GitHub adds three IP ranges for webhook deliveries
it.summary: Teams that maintain a static firewall allowlist for GitHub webhooks need to add three IP ranges to keep receiving deliveries. Teams that automatically sync their allowlists from GitHub's Meta API already pick up the additions.

it.title: Microsoft fixes Always On VPN failures in Windows 11
it.summary: Microsoft resolved the connection failures introduced by September's security updates after incorrectly marking the issue as fixed in October's cumulative updates.

it.title: Oracle Cloud will offer Google's AI chips
it.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure will become the first hyperscaler outside Google Cloud to offer Google's Tensor Processing Units.

hardware.title: Boom opens a $150M Colorado factory to build 42 MW gas turbines for AI data centers
hardware.summary: Boom opened a roughly 200,000-square-foot factory in Centennial, Colorado, to build Superpower, a 42 MW natural gas turbine for AI data centers, with deliveries targeted for mid-2027 and output rising to 25 turbines a year in 2028 and 50 in 2029. Superpower and the Overture airliner's Symphony engine are meant to share a core, and a prototype called Sprint Core is due for first firing before Thanksgiving. Launch customer Crusoe has since backed out of its 29-turbine order.

hardware.title: Samsung Foundry Confirms Hyperscaler 2nm Orders as First GAA Chips Enter Production
hardware.summary: Samsung confirmed new 2nm GAA chip production contracts with major cloud hyperscalers and AI companies during its Q3 2026 earnings call, marking a significant step in its foundry recovery. This move comes amid competition from TSMC, with Samsung emphasizing its first-to-market GAA transistor technology and improved yield rates. Samsung's foundry division remains unprofitable but expects future gains as it ramps up production and opens its US fab, aiming to capture market demand amidst supply constraints.

hardware.title: Google's Project Suncatcher Generates First AI Response in Orbit
hardware.summary: Project Suncatcher is a research effort by Google that aims to power AI compute in space. Its prototype satellite, launched on October 1, has now returned the first AI output from a data center-class TPU in orbit. A ground station uplinked a prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 model, and a haiku came back during a pass over Svalbard, Norway. Thermal stress and radiation tests come next, with two interconnected satellites planned for 2027.

hardware.title: Meta reportedly built a 106 lb household humanoid prototype with Fourier, running on Nvidia Jetson Thor
hardware.summary: Meta built a household humanoid prototype, codenamed Max, in about three months with Chinese robotics firm Fourier. It's about 1.5 m tall, runs on Nvidia Jetson Thor, and has a face display, speaker, and hands for small objects. Max 2, in work since September, redesigns the torso and hands and adds a projector and extra sensors for stairs. No launch date has been set.

hardware.title: The world model for real-world data
hardware.summary: Sensors and cameras capture the physical world, but interpreting this data means custom models: collect, train, tune, repeat. On Nov 5, discover how Archetype AI's Newton helps developers build agents that generalize across machines and run at the edge. Save your spot .

hardware.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers
hardware.summary: Satlyt's software successfully tested to distribute computing tasks among orbiting satellites on a NASA-funded project with the University of Houston. The software, already on three satellites, uses available compute resources and communication capacity to manage tasks, aiming to enhance data processing efficiency in space. Future plans include broader validation and integration, ultimately enabling developers to create space applications without rebuilding infrastructure for every mission.

hardware.title: SLAC confirms altermagnetism in manganese telluride with polarized X-rays, a magnet type aimed at spintronic memory
hardware.summary: Altermagnets are a third kind of magnet alongside ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Like antiferromagnets, they have no net magnetization, so stray fields can't flip them, but they can still carry spin-polarized currents, so their data can be read out. A SLAC-lead team shot polarized X-rays at maganese telluride and saw a directional signal that a conventional antiferromagnet can't produce. This work, published in Science, targets a usecase within spintronic memory.

hardware.title: Intel's Fab 28 explosion costs about $600M in revenue and squeezes 10nm Xeon supply into 2027
hardware.summary: On October 14, an explosion at Intel's Fab 28 in Kiryat Gat, Israel, killed two workers and halted the plant for about two weeks. The fab makes 10nm-class server chips such as Xeon 6 I/O dies, and Intel expects about $600 million in lost revenue across Q4 and Q1. Wafers take roughly six months to finish, so scrapped work delays supply into 2027 on top of an already tight server market.

hardware.title: China's embodied AI startups raised $13B in H1 2026, five times last year, as robot makers shift from moves to brains
hardware.summary: After years of building humanoids that run, dance, and backflip, Chinese companies are pouring money into the AI that would make them useful across more jobs, meaning software that lets robots understand their surroundings and learn new tasks without per-job programming. Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times a year earlier, with funding increasingly going to specialist robot-intelligence developers as well as manufacturers.

hardware.title: Altman says home AI inference wastes scarce DRAM and the cloud is the better use of it
hardware.summary: Sam Altman says that with silicon capacity constrained, it's poor global allocation for individuals to each hold a slice of the world's limited DRAM to run local models, and that utilization is highest in the cloud.

hardware.title: Toyota and Waymo Advance Autonomous Driving Collaboration for Safer Streets and Freedom of Movement for All
hardware.summary: Toyota and Waymo will test autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan by 2027 and expand to the UK and other markets later.

hardware.title: NASA asks industry about reboosting, servicing, or deorbiting Hubble by 2032
hardware.summary: NASA issued a Request for Information asking industry about reboosting Hubble to a higher orbit, servicing it, or disposing of it with a controlled reentry.

hardware.title: K2 Space targets 100 satellites a year and says a 165 kW satellite can host one compute rack
hardware.summary: K2 Space's CEO says it wants to build about 100 high-power satellites a year, after a $500 million round at roughly a $7 billion valuation, and that its 165 kW satellite is the size where hosting a compute rack becomes possible.
